ABSENCE: no `reset_drift_warnings()` in the autouse fixture, so _DRIFT_WARNED leaks between tests; correctness relies on pytest definition order

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish an intentional SKIP from accidental drift in resolve_outbound_status's stderr message (or suppress the alert for SKIP), so a deliberately-SKIPped status is not reported as drift.
evidence: outbound_mapper.py:61-69 warns for any target None: `if value not in _DRIFT_WARNED: ... print(f"rebar-reconciler: local status {value!r} has no Jira target ... (map-or-drift).")`
config.py:100 `return {k: v for k, v in resolved.status_map.items() if v != mc.SKIP}` — SKIP entries are dropped, so a deliberately-SKIPped status reaches resolve_outbound_status as an absent key
effective_status_map docstring (config.py:83-86) states a SKIP 'means the local status has NO Jira target — dropped here', i.e. SKIP and drift collapse to the same mapper-visible state
dropped.finding: resolve_outbound_status emits a 'drift' stderr alert for a status that the operator DELIBERATELY configured as SKIP, phrasing an intentional configuration choice as accidental drift ('has no Jira target ... leaving the Jira status field unchanged (map-or-drift)'). effective_status_map drops SKIP entries, so an intentional SKIP is indistinguishable at the mapper from an accidental omission and produces the same alarming warning.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm/handle the present-but-None status case so resolve_outbound_status is not invoked with value=None (e.g. coalesce None to 'open' at the call sites).
evidence: outbound_mapper.py:59-60 `effective = LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA if status_map is None else status_map; target = effective.get(value)` — value may be None
jira/outbound_fields.py: `resolve_outbound_status(ticket.get("status", "open"), status_map)` — .get(k, default) returns None when the key is present with value None
dropped.finding: resolve_outbound_status warns and dedupes on the raw local status value, so a ticket whose 'status' key is present-but-None (rather than defaulted to 'open') would call effective.get(None) -> None and emit a warning naming the local status as None. The create paths pass ticket.get('status', 'open'), which returns None when the key exists with a None value, bypassing the 'open' default.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the outbound mappers are only invoked single-threaded per process, or guard _DRIFT_WARNED against concurrent check-then-add.
evidence: outbound_mapper.py:44 `_DRIFT_WARNED: set[str] = set()` — module-global mutable shared state
outbound_mapper.py:62-63 `if value not in _DRIFT_WARNED: _DRIFT_WARNED.add(value)` — check-then-mutate is not atomic under concurrent callers
dropped.finding: _DRIFT_WARNED is a process-global mutable set mutated with a non-atomic check-then-add ('if value not in _DRIFT_WARNED: _DRIFT_WARNED.add(value)'). If the outbound mappers are ever invoked concurrently (multiple threads within one reconcile process), the dedupe could double-print or race on the shared set.
